title: International Students Receiving Tuition Grants and Their Employment Status after Graduation
what_it_is: International Students Receiving Tuition Grants and Their Employment Status after Graduation

sections.label: International students tuition grant bond obligations
sections.summary: About 2,900 tuition grant international students graduate yearly; most employed within three years, and defaulters face action preventing work or residence in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: From 2017 to 2023, on average, about 2,900 international students who received the Tuition Grant graduate each year from our polytechnics and autonomous universities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Within the first three years of graduating, more than eight in 10 are employed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Of the remainder, the majority are granted deferment for further studies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: We take the bond obligations of the international students on tuition grants seriously and we will pursue the international students who default on their obligations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: For those who fail to pay the liquidated damages, actions will be taken to prevent them from working or residing in Singapore.

sections.label: Deferment reasons and liquidated damages
sections.summary: Some cite health or lack of employment and are asked to pay liquidated damages; most deferments sought were for further studies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Some of them cite genuine reasons such as health and that they find could not employment in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: In those cases, we will ask them to pay the liquidated damages.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: As I have said earlier on, majority of deferments that were sought were based on the international students' request for further studies.
